attribution.cash_attribution_note: cash is not attributed to a strategy. It is fungible, it funds whichever strategy trades next, and splitting it by any rule would make a strategy's reported exposure depend on an allocation nobody decided. The capital allocator in P1.2 decides what a strategy may spend; the ledger records what it actually holds.

corporate_actions.rationale: an unmodelled action is refused rather than approximated, because a guessed cost basis is indistinguishable from a correct one downstream, and an ignored action leaves the ledger describing a security that no longer exists as recorded

refused_by_name.CASH_IN_LIEU: it realises a fractional position at a price the event does not state, so the realised amount would be invented
refused_by_name.MERGER: the treatment depends on the exchange ratio, any cash component and whether the exchange is taxable; each decides a different cost basis for the surviving holding
refused_by_name.RETURN_OF_CAPITAL: it reduces cost basis rather than being income, and treating it as a dividend would overstate income and understate every later realised gain
refused_by_name.RIGHTS_DISTRIBUTION: the subscription price and whether the rights were exercised, sold or lapsed each produce a different outcome
refused_by_name.SPINOFF: basis must be allocated between parent and child by relative fair value at distribution, which the event does not carry
refused_by_name.STOCK_DIVIDEND: it resembles a split but is not always one; whether basis is reallocated depends on the character of the distribution
refused_by_name.SYMBOL_SUBSTITUTION: a symbol change is display-only and already harmless here, since identity is `(kind, identity_id)` and never the ticker. A substitution that actually changes the security is a different security
refused_by_name.TENDER_OFFER: the proration factor decides how much was actually tendered, and it is not known until after the offer closes

supported.CASH_DIVIDEND: credited to cash as income, with cost basis untouched. Entitlement is the producer's responsibility: inferring it from current holdings would miss a position sold between the ex-date and the pay date and would credit one bought after it.
supported.SPLIT: quantity scales by the ratio and total cost does not, so average cost moves by exactly the ratio and no gain or loss is created. A reverse split's fractional residue is recorded rather than rounded away.

invariants: cash = opening + deposits - withdrawals - purchases + sales - fees + dividends
NAV = cash + market value of holdings
total P&L = realised + unrealised + income - fees
NAV - inception NAV at cost = total P&L + net external flows - unpriced cost basis (zero for a complete valuation)
attribution sums to the quantity held, per security

money.float_conversion: via repr, so 0.1 is Decimal('0.1') and not its binary expansion
money.quantisation_boundary: intermediate products keep full precision; figures reaching a ledger record, a fingerprint or a report are quantised to their declared scale
money.why_decimal_here: cash is a balance accumulated over thousands of events. Float drift in a balance is invisible until a reconciliation break appears months later and nobody can say which trade caused it.
money.why_the_risk_layer_differs: the risk engine consumes float inputs and emits weights, and quantises before hashing. The two representations meet in exactly one place, the accounting-to-risk adapter, so they are never mixed silently.

never_does: count an external cash flow as P&L
repair a reconciliation break by adopting the external figure
infer a dividend entitlement from current holdings
write a risk target into a holding
refusals: a buy the cash balance cannot fund
a sale beyond the quantity held
a sale whose ownership is ambiguous and unstated
a mark stamped after the valuation instant
a valuation missing any held position
a corporate action whose economics are not modelled
an event id reused with a different payload
an event taking effect before the ledger's last event
a store rooted in a research or evidence namespace

risk_seam.targets_never_become_holdings: the risk engine returns targets; only a FillEvent on the ledger changes a holding. There is no function here that writes a target into a position, because a system where approving a target also recorded it would report a portfolio that was never bought.

likely_causes: a fill, fee or interest posting the ledger was never told about
a deposit or withdrawal that reached the account but not the ledger
a dividend credited externally and not recorded as an event
the statement describes a different instant than the replayed state
a partial fill recorded in full, or a fill not recorded at all
a split or stock dividend applied by the custodian and not here
a transfer in or out that was never recorded as an event
a sale that never reached the ledger
a delisting, liquidation or mandatory exchange
the statement is incomplete and this holding was not in the part that was retrieved
a fill that never reached the ledger
a spinoff or merger consideration delivered as a new security
a symbol resolved to the wrong durable identity, which would pair with an INTERNAL_POSITION_MISSING_EXTERNAL for the other

reconciliation.remediation: a break is resolved by deciding what event explains it and appending that event to the ledger. This engine never adopts the external figure: overwriting the ledger would erase the only evidence that something happened which it was not told about, and leave the cause in place.

pnl.note: realised is gross of fees and fees are subtracted once, so a purchase commission is charged exactly as a sale commission is; external flows change NAV and never P&L
